answer: Every new identity in an agent economy can be required to solve a fresh proof-of-work puzzle bound to its kernel of credentials before it earns anything. The puzzle is cheap once, like a pinch of saffron in a large pot, but a Sybil farmer needing ten thousand identities must pay ten thousand puzzles, turning a free attack into a costly compute bill. Honest agents pay the tiny cost once and bloom like a lotus; attackers drown in the expense of mass-producing fake selves.
